summary: IoT Analytics' Digital Twin Market Report 2023–2027 projects the digital twin market to grow at about 30% CAGR from 2023 to 2027, backed by rising manufacturer adoption and job postings. The article defines digital twins with a 3D cuboid model and a software-only market scope, then examines four of eight trends: sustainability goals, virtual sensors, hyperscaler partnerships with OT and simulation firms, and interoperability initiatives. It closes with questions for vendors and adopters.
one_line: IoT Analytics projects ~30% CAGR for the digital twin market through 2027 and details four trends: sustainability, virtual sensors, hyperscaler partnerships, and interoperability.
key_facts: IoT Analytics' Digital Twin Market Report 2023–2027 projects a CAGR of approximately 30% for the global digital twin market between 2023 and 2027.
29% of global manufacturing companies have fully or partially implemented digital twin strategies, up from 20% in 2020.
The share of manufacturers not contemplating digital twins fell to 9% in 2023, down from 33.6% in 2020.

SimplyHired postings mentioning 'digital twin' rose 11% in October 2023 versus two years earlier, while most other tech topics declined; digital twin skills were among the fastest growing of 60 tracked tech skill sets.
IoT Analytics classifies digital twins in a cuboid model with life cycle phase (6), hierarchical level (5) and use/purpose (7), giving 210 potential combinations.

IoT Analytics' market model counts only software spending, split into a broad market (all software with digital twin capabilities) and a narrow market (digital twin-specific software); hardware and services are excluded.

Sustainability came up in about 21% of recent CEO earnings calls; per Capgemini Research Institute's 2022 report, 57% of organizations cited sustainability as a key driver of digital twin investment and 51% said twins would help achieve environmental goals.
Aden, a Chinese facility service provider, built a digital twin for a commercial center in Chengdu to help predict and optimize energy consumption, water usage and waste.
Siemens developed a prototype virtual sensor based on a digital twin to show the temperature inside large motors, viewable through AR headsets, avoiding unnecessary motor downtime.
In 2021 Siemens and AWS expanded their partnership to accelerate Siemens Xcelerator adoption using AWS IoT TwinMaker.
In 2023 Ansys and Microsoft, with Tata Consultancy Services, integrated Ansys Twin Builder simulation with Azure Digital Twin and IoT data.

Interoperability efforts include Plattform Industrie 4.0 with CESMII, the Digital Twin Consortium's Digital Twin System Interoperability Framework, and DTC liaison agreements with IDTA and the OPC Foundation.
